::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 20th [1869]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 227-8
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
Many thanks, it is very agreeable to get anything out of [America](organizations/other_172.qmd). I have a [story](cmy_books/cmybook_81.qmd) of the time of Henry V and James I of Scotland - about half out in the [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd), and all written. I was thinking of proposing it to you for Christmas when it will be finished in the Monthly Packet. Might not some arrangement be made about it with [Scribner](organizations/other_204.qmd). I could either send them the numbers already in type the MP - or they might be printed at once, and the duplicate sheets sent up to the end. I do not think we ever came to any agreement about the [Chaplet](cmy_books/cmybook_69.qmd) itself - whether you give me £200 as before for the first edition.

I do not know what has become of the proof of the [Parallel History](cmy_books/cmybook_89.qmd). The printers sent me the copy, evidently printed from but no proofs with it.

What do you think about a volume of essay kind of papers? I have done a few at times for the [Christian Remembrancer](organizations/other_59.qmd), [one](cmy_books/cmybook_302.qmd) on Miss Sewell’s [principles of education](other_books/otherbook_548.qmd) - one on [Folklore](cmy_books/cmybook_65.qmd), an [account of the Sanitary Commission](cmy_books/cmybook_303.qmd) in the American war, a [life of Lord Seaton](cmy_books/cmybook_66.qmd), and a few more which are in the [Literary Churchman](organizations/other_76.qmd) - they seem to me some of them rather worth saving, but they would <u>keep</u>. I have likewise in MS a nearly completed essay on or rather history of literature for children, which I should add to those. It is too long for the [Magazine](organizations/other_78.qmd), and not at all in the same tone.[^1]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: Nevertheless Macmillan was to publish it in his magazine, in three parts: 'Children’s literature of the last century: I. - Nursery books of the eighteenth century.'; Children’s literature of the last century: II. - Didactic fiction.'; and 'Children’s literature of the last century: III. - Class literature of the last thirty years.'
